properties.description: Originally a Punic mine, Riotinto was one of the largest mines in the Roman empire. It may be the site that Ptolemy refers to as Urium. Silver and copper mine which produced an estimated 16,000,000 tons of slag. 16 pairs of water wheels found in the mine draining depths of 100m. It is surrounded by an extensive settlement with cemeteries.

properties.description: A large Roman mine noted for its many shafts - 100 twin shafts and 50 single shafts. To drain the mines water-lifting devices were used; remains of an Archimedes screw and a pump have been found. Smelting activities produced an estimated 40,000 tons of slag.

properties.description: Extraction started at Tharsis in the Iron Age, circa 2500 BC. The zenith of production was under Trajan but coins which have been found suggest mining could have continued until AD 350. The site has large slag piles and an estimated 4,000,000 tonnes of slag were produced. Other finds include remains of a water wheel with a rope still attached. After the Visigoths invaded the difficulty in draining the mine may have made it unworkable and been the cause of its closure.
